title.narrative: UNODC- Enhancing the RoL and Criminal Justice System in Eth - 2023 - 2026
UNODC- Enhancing the RoL and Criminal Justice System in Eth - 2023 - 2026

description.narrative:
Samarbetspartner är United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) som är en aktiv medlem i United Nations Country Team (UNCT) i Etiopien. Det är en känd partner till Sverige och har genomfört ett program finansierat av Sverige mellan 2014 2022. Sveriges djupgående analys av institutionell uppbyggnad av några av dess bidrag har också avslöjat att UNODC personal har byggt upp starka relationer med viktiga samtalspartner inom regeringen som säkerställer det samarbete som behövs vid genomförandet av projektet.
Detta ingripande är något en fortsättning på den tidigare fasen av UNODC program för att reformera Etiopiens straffrättssystem i syfte att göra straffrättssystemen mer effektiva och ansvarsfulla genom stärkt tillgång till rättvisa för alla med fokus på utsatta grupper.
Sverige stödjer detta projekt med 36 MSEK under fyra år från 2023 till 2026, vilket kommer att gå under UNODC paraplylandsprogram.

The cooperation partner is the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) that is an active member of the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) in Ethiopia. It is a known partner to Sweden and has been implementing a program funded by Sweden between 2014 2022. Sweden's deep-dive analysis on institutional building of some of its contributions have also revealed that UNODC's staff have built strong relationship with key interlocutors within the government that ensures the cooperation needed in the implementation of the project.
This intervention is somewhat a continuation of the previous phase of UNODC’s programme in reforming the Criminal Justice System of Ethiopia with the aim of making criminal justice systems more effective and accountable by strengthened access to justice for all with a focus on vulnerable groups.
Sweden is supporting this project with 36 MSEK over four years from 2023 to 2026, which will go under the umbrella country program of UNODC.

The intervention aims to contribute to building peaceful, just and inclusive societies by attempting to address the problem of crime.
The overall objective of the intervention is to enhance rule of law and integrity in the administration of criminal justice system through strengthening capacity, accountability and coordination in Ethiopia.
UNODC understands integrity in the form of institutional integrity in the context of criminal justice institutions and other actors. In this sense, integrity is linked with concepts of accountability and oversight. For instance, the UNODC Handbook on police accountability, oversight and integrity (2011) defines police integrity as normative and other safeguards that keep police from misusing their powers and abusing their rights and privileges and accountability as a system of internal and external checks and balances aimed at ensuring that police carry out their duties properly and are held responsible if they fail to do so. Such a system is meant to uphold police integrity and deter misconduct and to restore or enhance public confidence in policing. Similarly, judicial integrity and prosecutorial integrity are concepts closely linked with accountability and professionalism.
Moreover, the specific objective of the planned intervention is to:
Support the criminal justice systems to be more effective and accountable by strengthened access to justice for all through more effective, fair and accountable criminal justice systems with a focus on vulnerable groups.
Planned outcomes to achieve the objective include:
Outcome 1. Ethiopias law enforcement and intergovernmental/regional cooperation is improved
Outcome 2. The Ethiopian justice system is more accountable, effective and independent
Outcome 3. Rehabilitative approaches to prison management are adopted
Target Groups
The planned intervention will work closely with the core criminal justice institutions and government bodies with relevant mandates as well the respective regional counterparts. Targeted stakeholders include the Ethiopian Federal Police Commission, Ethiopian Police University, Ministry of Justice, Federal Supreme Court, Federal Prison Commission, Prison Commission Training Center, and Ministry of Women and Social Affairs.
The intervention aims to support criminal justice institutions, systems and mechanisms to function more effectively to be able to prevent and tackle crime and ensuring accountability thereby contributing to access to justice for all. The short-term contribution of the various capacity building, harmonization of legislation and crime prevention activities implemented by this project is improved service delivery in terms of quality and access, and contribution to the achievement of the SDGs, which will themselves be conducive to supporting rule of law and integrity in the criminal justice system in Ethiopia as well as preventing and tackling crime.
Moreover, the cooperation partner will work with UN entities with related mandates, civil society networks, young women and men, grassroots women and the private sector to engage them in planning as well as monitoring services delivered by government.

Examples of Results
Human Rights Audit of Police Curriculum Conducted and New Curriculum on Transnational Organized Crime Developed: A human rights audit of the Ethiopian Police Universitys existing curriculum was conducted and validated to identify gaps in human rights integration and training modules related to crime prevention and investigation. In parallel, support was provided for the development of a new curriculum on transnational organized crime, with particular attention to trafficking in persons. The process identified priority areas for further support to strengthen human rights-based and specialized police training.
Women Police Leaders Leadership Capacity Strengthened: Thirty-three senior and mid-level female police officers received leadership training to strengthen their leadership skills and promote democratic policing, human rights-based approaches, and the protection of vulnerable groups.
High-Level Forum Convened to Revitalize Implementation of National Crime Prevention Strategy: A high-level forum was convened to address challenges affecting the implementation of Ethiopias National Crime Prevention Strategy and identify practical measures to strengthen coordination and operationalization. The forum brought together key justice and governance actors to improve collaboration and advance implementation of the Strategy.
Improving Crime Data Management through National Statistics Study: A study on crime statistics and data management was conducted to assess existing crime data recording practices, identify gaps, and propose measures to strengthen the accuracy, consistency, and use of crime-related information across federal and regional law enforcement institutions.
National Strategy on Transnational Organized Crime Drafted and Validated: A draft national strategy on transnational organized crime was developed and validated through consultations with relevant justice and security stakeholders. Ministry of Justice (MoJ), with continued technical support, is undertaking the final drafting process to incorporate consultation inputs and prepare the strategy for submission to the Council of Ministers for adoption.
New Arms Control Proclamation Drafted: A draft Arms Control Proclamation was developed to strengthen Ethiopias legal framework on arms control; address identified gaps and replace the existing proclamation. The draft has been submitted to the Ministry of Justice for further review and stakeholder consultation before adoption.
Two Federal Judiciary Proclamation Bills Revised: Draft amendments to the Federal Courts Proclamation and the Federal Judicial Administration Proclamation were developed to strengthen the effectiveness, accountability, and independence of Ethiopias federal judiciary. The revised bills are awaiting approval by the House of Peoples Representatives.
Asset Recovery Proclamation Implementation Discussed: A stakeholder panel discussion was conducted to promote understanding of Ethiopias new asset recovery legal framework, which introduces a new paradigm for asset recovery in the country. The event brought together prosecutors and other relevant actors involved in financial investigations, asset recovery, and anti-money laundering to discuss implementation challenges, international practices, and practical issues arising from the application of the Asset Recovery Proclamation enacted in 2025.
Capacity of Justice Actors Strengthened on New Asset Recovery Framework: A stakeholder dialogue and a series of training workshops were conducted to promote understanding and implementation of Ethiopias new asset recovery framework introduced through the Asset Recovery Proclamation enacted in 2025. The new framework represents a new paradigm for asset recovery in Ethiopia, and the sessions provided a platform to discuss key legal provisions, implementation challenges, international practices, and related instruments. The activities brought together prosecutors, asset recovery officials, and federal judges to exchange experiences and build a common understanding of the requirements and practical application of the new regime.
Capacity of Federal and Regional Prosecutors Strengthened on Corruption Crimes:A specialized training programme was conducted for federal and regional prosecutors to strengthen understanding of Ethiopias anti-corruption legal framework, including relevant provisions of the new Asset Recovery Proclamation, sentencing guidelines, and international anti-corruption standards. The training provided a platform for experience sharing and discussion on the application of corruption laws across jurisdictions.
Capacity of Prosecutors Strengthened on Gender-Based Violence Prosecution: A specialized training programme was conducted for federal and regional prosecutors to strengthen understanding of Ethiopias legal framework on gender-based violence, international standards, victim-centered approaches, and measures to reduce secondary victimization. The training also provided practical exposure to survivor-centered service delivery through a visit to the UNODC-supported GBV Centre at the Yirgalem Integrated Agro-Industrial Park.
Criminal Justice Administration Strategy for Young Offenders and Diversion Drafted: A draft Criminal Justice Administration Strategy for Young Offenders and Diversion was developed to strengthen child-sensitive approaches within Ethiopias criminal justice system, including the use of diversion measures for children in conflict with the law. The strategy aligns with the National Crime Prevention Strategy and has undergone stakeholder consultations. It is currently under review before submission to the Council of Ministers for approval.
Judicial Lessons from Sweden Twinning Mission Shared: A debriefing and experience-sharing session was conducted following the judicial twinning mission to Sweden to document and disseminate lessons learned among judges and court leadership. The session supported institutional learning and informed ongoing judicial reform efforts within the Federal Supreme Court.
Proclamation on the Reintegration of Inmates Drafted: A draft proclamation on the reintegration of inmates was developed to establish a legal framework for supporting the social reintegration of individuals after release from prison. The proposed legislation addresses a key gap in Ethiopias criminal justice system by providing a framework for post-release support and has been submitted to the Council of Ministers for deliberation and approval.
Proclamation on Alternatives to Incarceration Drafted: A draft proclamation on alternatives to incarceration was developed to introduce more rehabilitative and proportionate sentencing approaches within Ethiopias criminal justice system. The proposed legislation aims to reduce reliance on imprisonment by establishing alternative measures and has been refined through stakeholder consultations before submission for consideration by the Council of Ministers.
Capacity of Prison Officials Strengthened on Drug Prevention and Treatment: A series of trainings was conducted to strengthen prison officials understanding of drug dependence, mental health, and rehabilitation approaches in correctional settings. The programme promoted evidence-based approaches to addiction treatment, mental health support, and the links between substance use, crime prevention, and public health, contributing to a more rehabilitative approach to prison management in Ethiopia.
Capacity of Prison Officers Strengthened on the Rights of Women in Detention: A national training programme was conducted to strengthen prison officers understanding of international standards on the treatment of women deprived of liberty, including the Nelson Mandela Rules and the Bangkok Rules. The training promoted gender-responsive prison management, prevention of gender-based violence, and improved access to essential services for women in detention, while encouraging experience sharing and practical actions to improve detention conditions.
Federal and Regional Prison Administrations Joint Consultation Forum Convened: The 18th Federal and Regional Prison Administration Joint Consultation Forum was convened to review progress on prison reform commitments, discuss management challenges and good practices, and promote the application of international standards. The forum provided a platform for prison authorities and justice sector stakeholders to exchange experiences and discuss priorities related to prison management modernization, institutional coordination, and ongoing legislative reforms.
Participation in International Association of Prosecutors Annual Conference: Ethiopian prosecutors participated in the 30th Annual Conference of the International Association of Prosecutors, providing an opportunity to exchange experiences on international cooperation, organized crime, corruption, asset recovery, and the use of technology in prosecution. The engagement exposed prosecutors to international standards and emerging practices relevant to strengthening prosecution services.
Participation in Expert Group Meeting on the Use of Technology in Prisons: Ethiopian prison officials participated in the Expert Group Meeting on the Use of Technology in Prisons, contributing to discussions on international guidance for technology use in correctional settings. The engagement provided exposure to international standards and innovative prison management practices relevant to Ethiopias ongoing efforts to modernize correctional services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
